patients.summary: Retired teacher with diabetes, CKD, COPD, CAD and gastroparesis who joins in 2020 with her daughter. Over six years: Alzheimer's diagnosis, pelvic prolapse managed with a pessary, a high-risk pancreatic cyst under surveillance, metoclopramide parkinsonism, an HHS admission, pneumonia with AKI, a right hip fracture and, after her last visit, an inferior STEMI.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
72 y/o retired grade-school teacher here to establish. Came with her daughter, who does most of the talking about logistics. Previous PCP retired; records requested today.

History by report: type 2 diabetes for many years, on metformin and bedtime glargine, does not check sugars often. Blood pressure and cholesterol treated for years. Told she has COPD; uses a once-daily inhaler, no recent flares or steroid courses. Kidney function 'a bit low' per prior doctor. Osteoporosis on a bone scan last year, nothing prescribed she can remember. Heart: says she had an abnormal stress test some years back and was managed with pills, no stent, no heart attack. Stomach empties slowly from the diabetes; takes metoclopramide before meals and nausea is mostly controlled.

Daughter mentions Mom repeats herself and misplaces things more than she used to; both feel it is about age. Lives on her own, drives short distances, manages her own pills.

Meds reviewed bottle by bottle: metformin 1000 BID, glargine 24 u at bedtime, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, metoclopramide 10 TID ac.
Allergies: none known.
Surgical: none major.
Family: mother type 2 diabetes and breast cancer; father coronary disease; sister with Alzheimer's.
Social: quit cigarettes around 2004. No alcohol. Widowed.

Exam: pleasant, conversant, somewhat vague on dates. Weight and BP as recorded. Lungs with mildly diminished breath sounds at bases, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, monofilament sensation intact, pulses present. No edema.

Assessment and plan:
1. Type 2 diabetes: A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Same regimen pending numbers.
2. Hypertension: a little above goal today; recheck at follow-up before changing anything.
3. CKD 3a by history: recheck creatinine, avoid NSAIDs.
4. Hyperlipidemia/CAD: lipids today; aspirin and statin continue.
5. COPD: stable on tiotropium.
6. Gastroparesis: on metoclopramide per prior team.
7. Osteoporosis: will look at the DXA when records come.
8. Memory: mild per family; will follow.
9. Health maintenance: Tdap today, hep C screen today, flu next month when high-dose arrives. Mammogram to be ordered.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Frances (and family) - your labs from Tuesday are back. Sugar average (A1c) is in a reasonable range for you, kidney numbers match the mild chronic kidney disease we talked about, cholesterol is at goal on atorvastatin, and the hepatitis C screen is negative. No changes. I've put in an order for your mammogram; the imaging center will call to schedule.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
38 pages received from previous primary care office. Abstracted for PCP:
- 2016 exercise nuclear stress test: abnormal, consistent with coronary artery disease; cardiology recommended medical therapy, no catheterization.
- 2018 spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.64, FEV1 66% predicted, consistent with COPD.
- 2019 DXA: lowest T-score -2.6 at the left femoral neck, osteoporosis.
- 2019 gastric emptying study: delayed emptying; metoclopramide 10 mg before meals started by her prior physician that year.
- 2016 colonoscopy: normal, no repeat advised given age.
- 2012 Pap: normal; screening discontinued after that.
- 2019 screening mammogram: benign.
- Problem and medication lists match what she brought on 9/22.
Scanned to media. PCP reviewed.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up diabetes/HTN. Daughter along. Took her glargine every night per daughter's check of the pen count. Occasional morning nausea, better if she eats small amounts. No hypoglycemia symptoms. Breathing at her usual, one inhaler.
Exam: no distress. Chest with distant sounds, no wheeze. RRR. No edema.
Plan: A1c and BMP today, regimen unchanged. COVID vaccine: eligible now by age; daughter is signing her up through a pharmacy. Back in about 4 months for her wellness visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wellness visit. Health risk questionnaire done with daughter's help.
Function: bathes, dresses, cooks simple meals on her own; daughter handles bills now. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine for conversation, glasses for reading.
Mood: PHQ-2 negative.
Cognition: recall 2 of 3 words; daughter thinks things are stable since fall. Will keep watching.
Prevention: mammogram done November, normal. Colonoscopy 2016 normal, no further screening at her age. Pap screening ended. Tdap 2020, flu 2020, COVID x2, Shingrix #1 in March with #2 booked. Pneumococcal: will give the newer conjugate vaccine this fall.
Vitals reviewed. Exam: well-appearing, lungs without wheeze, heart regular, no edema.
Plan: continue meds. Diabetes follow-up next month with labs.

documents.title: Chronic care follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for diabetes, BP, kidneys. Summer was quiet.
ROS: no chest pain, breathing at baseline, no new GI symptoms beyond occasional nausea.
Exam: comfortable. Chest clear, a little diminished. Regular rhythm. Monofilament normal both feet, no ulcers. No swelling.
Plan: yearly bloods today (CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin). Flu, PCV20 and COVID booster next month. Discussed whether memory slips are increasing - daughter not sure yet, will watch.

documents.title: Memory concerns
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter asked for this visit and spoke with me first while the MA roomed her mother.
Her account: the forgetting has been building for roughly two years and has clearly sped up. Mom misses appointments even with a calendar, forgets whole phone conversations, asks the same questions within minutes. She has pulled back from church friends and her book group. Late afternoons and evenings she gets irritable and restless. In the last few weeks she has accused the cleaning person and a neighbor of taking money and jewelry; the items turn up in drawers.
Patient herself says her memory is 'fine for my age' and is annoyed by the topic, though not hostile.
No head injury, no new meds, no alcohol. Sleeping OK. Eating OK.
Exam: alert, cooperative but flat. Knows her name and the town, not the date or the month. Speech fluent. No focal weakness, gait steady. Vitals as recorded.
Assessment: progressive cognitive decline with behavioral changes and paranoid ideas, likely a neurodegenerative dementia; rule out reversible contributors.
Plan: BMP with calcium, TSH, B12 today. Neurology referral for formal evaluation, daughter to attend. Talked with daughter about driving - she will take the car keys for now and Mom agreed for the winter.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results are in: sodium 142, calcium 9.2, kidney function stable (creatinine 1.0), sugar 140 non-fasting, thyroid 2.5 and B12 both normal. Nothing here explains the memory changes, which is what we expected. The neurology office has the referral and these results.

documents.body: Annual dilated exam 12/7/2021. Acuity stable. Early cataract changes, not visually significant. No retinopathy OU. No macular edema. Recheck in 12 months. NKDA.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology consultation, visit date 12/24/2021. Received by fax.

Reason: cognitive decline, referred by PCP.
Thank you for sending Ms. Mayhew, 73, seen with her daughter. Per the daughter, recall for recent events (appointments, conversations) has slipped steadily over about two years. She has become quieter and less engaged, with evening irritability, and recently insists that people are taking her belongings, which family has not found to be true.
Background: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, CKD stage 3, hyperlipidemia, osteoporosis, CAD, gastroparesis. No surgeries. Medications: metformin, insulin glargine 24 units nightly, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin 81, tiotropium, metoclopramide 10 mg before meals. Allergies: NKDA. Family: sister with Alzheimer's disease; mother diabetes; father CAD. Former smoker, quit about 20 years ago; no alcohol; retired teacher.
Exam: awake and attentive but apathetic. Oriented to self only, not to date or place. MMSE 18/30. Cranial nerves, strength, reflexes, sensation and coordination without focal findings.
Data: PCP labs from 11/23 reviewed - glucose 140, sodium 142, creatinine 1.0, calcium 9.2, TSH 2.5, B12 normal.
Impression: dementia of the Alzheimer type, moderate range by MMSE, with behavioral features (apathy, sundowning, misidentification/theft beliefs).
Plan: start donepezil 5 mg at bedtime, increase to 10 mg at 6-8 weeks if tolerated. MRI brain without contrast. Avoid antipsychotics for the delusional thinking for now; redirection strategies reviewed with daughter. Follow-up in about 10 weeks.
